author: Jennifer Miller
title: Columbia County Fall Fair opens Thursday with rides, food and shows - NewsBreak
text:
By Jennifer Miller ,
20 hours ago
It's county fair season and the annual Columbia County Fall Fair opens Thursday with rides, thrills, entertainment, and plenty of fair food.
The annual event put on by the Merchants Association of Columbia County opens at 5 p.m. at the fairgrounds at 5462 Columbia Road in Grovetown. It continues through Nov. 15.
The popular Demolition Derby will be back at the fair this year beginning at 7:30 p.m. on Nov. 9 and 13. And on Nov. 14, all rides are free from noon to 1 p.m.
There will also be plenty of exhibitions for all ages, including a large wild animal and taxidermy display at the Golabchi Educational Center at the fairgrounds that's included in the admission fee. For the center's hours, visit columbiacountyfair.net/events/fall-fair/fall-fair-events-calendar .
On Nov. 15, the popular local duo Little Roy and Lizzy will perform at 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. The musical duo from Lincolnton is known for their bluegrass and country music. The Eudora Petting Zoo will have plenty of animals to pet.
Admission to the fair is $10, with anyone 6 and under getting in free. Unlimited ride tickets are $25 Monday through Thursday, and $30 on Friday through Sunday. The minimum height to ride is 36 inches.
On opening day, the first 250 people at the gate get in free as part of the America 250 celebration. On Nov. 11, military members get in for $2.50 in honor of Veterans Day.
Fair-goers should be aware of fair rules this year, according to the fair's website. Those include:
After 7 p.m., no one younger than 17 will be admitted to the fair without a parent or guardian who can show a valid ID.
Each parent or guardian can bring a maximum of four children.
There will be no re-entry to the fairgrounds after 9 p.m.
Anyone with improper attire may be asked to leave the fairgrounds. No profanity is allowed on clothing or other items. Pants must be worn at the waist, and short shorts or revealing attire is not permitted.
Only clear bags can be brought onto the fairgrounds. Diaper bags will be subject to search.
Face masks are not permitted.
The fair will be open from 5-10 p.m. Monday through Thursday, from 5-11 p.m. on Fridays, from noon to 11 p.m. on Saturdays, and from 1-10 p.m. on Sundays. For more information, visit www.columbiacountyfair.net .
Jennifer Miller covers food and business for The Augusta Chronicle. She can be reached at jmiller@USATodayco.com.
